deps.name: newton
deps.why: Alloy uses Newton 1.8 APIs (coupled solvers, compact soft contacts) that no final release has yet, plus eleven VBD cloth and contact commits and the N-solver proxy coupling of ours on top of the public release-1.8 branch (2026-11-09, five days after 1.8.0rc1). The commit ships inside the alloy-engine wheel as alloy/_vendor/newton (its LICENSE, NOTICE and SPDX headers kept), so installing Alloy never installs or touches a separate newton package.

patches.why: the dihedral bending force of hinges with triangles under about 1 mm was dropped (degeneracy test was absolute)
edge/face soft contacts over-relaxed with a squared barycentric weight; a clamped sheet chattered and lost most of its friction at 10-20 iterations
tests for the lumped corner Hessian
self-contact stiffness jumped from 0 to full at the contact distance; resting cloth layers jittered
tests aligned with the lumped corner Hessian (tests only; the attachment test is upstream's rewrite from #5146)
the out-of-plane stiffness of the membrane Hessian made flat cloth converge very slowly out of plane
keeps the clamped normal stiffness for cloth pieces in contact (the exact value broke gripper pinches and resting film); ported onto release-1.8's accumulate_elasticity_force_and_hessian
a pinned sheet with stiff hinges settled past its static equilibrium at finite iterations (inertial start x + h*v + h^2*a_ext); pinned pieces start from x + h*v
a fold resting near +-pi read a 2*pi bending-angle difference and got a wrong-way torque (jitter on folds and seams)
couple more than two solvers over an acyclic proxy graph (SolverCoupledProxy): robot -> soft body -> liquid chains

routes.vendored: shipped inside alloy-engine as alloy/_vendor/newton; no separate newton wheel
routes.release: public newton==1.8.0 from PyPI once final, with the unmerged commits upstreamed or vendored (paused)
routes.wait: #5146 is upstream and in the base; #5131 is open; nine commits are not posted

dropped.why: attachment forces in the deterministic VBD contact gather: merged upstream and in release-1.8, so the base carries it

deps.name: mujoco-warp
deps.why: release v3.17.0, the MuJoCo Warp that Newton release-1.8 is built against (its eq_data is 12 wide, MuJoCo 3.17's layout). Files unchanged; it ships inside the alloy-engine wheel as alloy/_vendor/mujoco_warp (LICENSE and SPDX headers kept) so its Warp kernels carry Alloy's own names and a mujoco-warp of the user's is left alone. Alloy patches it at run time (the EPA of the unmerged mujoco_warp#1845, the ordered route).

routes.vendored: shipped inside alloy-engine as alloy/_vendor/mujoco_warp; no separate mujoco-warp wheel
routes.release: mujoco-warp==3.17.0 on PyPI is the same code; requiring it instead would share Warp kernels with the user's copy and tie the run-time patches to whatever version is installed

deps.name: mujoco
where: pyproject.toml (the vendored Newton release-1.8 and MuJoCo Warp v3.17.0 need MuJoCo 3.17)
deps.why: MuJoCo C: MJCF loading, the CPU route for rigid bodies and robots, and CPU cross-checks. 3.17.0 is the version the vendored Newton release-1.8 and MuJoCo Warp v3.17.0 are built against (3.16 fails every MuJoCo-routed scene: eq_data is 11 wide there)

deps.name: warp-lang
deps.why: the GPU kernel language under Newton and MuJoCo Warp; 1.18.0 is what every Alloy result ran on

routes.vendored: warp-lang==1.18.0 from PyPI (1.19.0 is newer and untested with Alloy)

deps.name: pytetwild
deps.why: tetrahedral meshing for soft bodies; 0.3+ imports pyvista at import time without declaring it

routes.release: keep the exact pin in the [mesh] extra
